claim.quote: The upper limit of the effective electron neutrino mass is improved by almost a factor 2 compared to the lowest current value [2], reaching mνe < 15 eV/c2 (90% credible interval).

date.note: arXiv v1 date; no journal reference was found in the abstract page consulted.

name: Improved limit on the effective electron neutrino mass with the ECHo-1k experiment

summary.plain: Using about 200 million holmium-163 decays recorded with ultra-cold detectors, ECHo found no neutrino mass signal and limits the electron neutrino mass to 15 electron-volts. It also measured the decay energy, 2862 eV, matching an independent Penning-trap value.
summary.technical: ECHo-1k spectrum of about 2×10⁸ events with background 9.1×10⁻⁶ /eV/pixel/day: endpoint Q = 2862(4) eV (Penning trap: 2863.2(6) eV) and m(νe) < 15 eV/c² (90% credible interval), almost a factor 2 better than the previous lowest calorimetric value.

title: Improved limit on the effective electron neutrino mass with the ECHo-1k experiment
why_it_matters: Brings calorimetric 163Ho measurements to the 10 eV scale, an independent cross-check of tritium-based neutrino-mass limits and the stepping stone to ECHo-100k.
